prerequisites: Prior knowledge of signals and systems in continuous and discrete variables is recommended.
A solid foundation in algebra and statistics is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Understanding and mastering the basic concepts of information theory, signals, and systems, used in different schemes and techniques of data representation and manipulation.
Ability to analyze, encode, process and transmit information and data using signal processing techniques.
Know how to apply filtering techniques and design digital filters.
Know how to design statistical estimators for parameters and signals.
Know how to describe an image, audio or video signal at the content level by its different local or frequency characteristics.
Know how to implement methods based on knowledge of theoretical foundations, algorithms and standards for audio and video encoding and compression.
Know how to evaluate the suitability of applied methodologies in specific audiovisual processing problems.
Recognize the aspects present in a basic image acquisition model and the processes involved in the generation and processing of a digital image.
Recognize and apply the fundamentals, formats and techniques of video processing and filtering.
Design and implement algorithms for sound processing applying signal representation techniques, digital synthesis, spectral analysis and sound transformation.

syllabus_topics: Information of continuous and discrete nature. Encoding of information in signals. Sampling of continuous signals: analysis in real domain and transformed domains. Decimation and interpolation.
Systems for analog and digital processing. Representation of continuous systems by digital systems. Representation of digital systems by continuous systems.

Digital filters: design and characterization. Definition of digital systems by difference equations. FIR and IIR systems. Impulse response, frequency response and system function of a digital filter. Design and characterization of filters in the Z domain. Structures for digital filters.
Analysis of deterministic and random signals: analysis of the properties of signals in the real domain and in transformed domains.
Optimal filtering, adaptive systems and regression. Calculation of optimal filters. Adaptive systems: LMS algorithm and its variants. Other iterative and adaptive algorithms.

Voice and audio processing. Voice and audio signals: properties. Voice encoding. Image and Video processing. Discrete cosine transform. Fundamentals, formats and techniques of video processing and filtering. Theoretical foundations, algorithms and standards for audio and video encoding and compression.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary assessment, a minimum of 3 out of 10 points must be obtained in the final exam (E1). If all minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as (0.40*E1 + 0.45*T1 + 0.15*P1). Otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. For the extraordinary assessment, the final grade is calculated as (0.40*E1 + 0.60*P1) with a minimum of 3 out of 10 in E1. Students may keep their T1 and P1 grades from the ordinary assessment, with these replacing P1 in the extraordinary assessment.
